before:
The benchmark was implemented in Python. The same fitted network
generated $1{,}000$ training-length and then $1{,}000$ holdout-length
paths, in that order, from one random stream seeded with $1234$ for
NumPy and PyTorch, so the order is part of the reproduction recipe.
after:
The Python benchmark seeded NumPy and PyTorch with $1234$ before
training. Generation then used the continuing NumPy stream, without
reseeding, for $1{,}000$ training-length paths followed by $1{,}000$
holdout-length paths from the same fitted network.

before:
Each state's dwell
time is negative binomial, fitted by the method of moments when the
state has at least five visits with overdispersed lengths, and
geometric otherwise, and its emissions are Student-$t$ with $\nu = 5$.
after:
For each state, we fitted a negative-binomial count distribution
by moments of the observed visit lengths when at least five visits
had mean length above $1.01$ and variance above the mean, using a
geometric fallback otherwise. The simulator added one to each
nonnegative count to obtain a positive dwell time; fitting used the
unshifted visit lengths. Emissions were Student-$t$ with $\nu = 5$.

before:

little.
after:
Thus, the controlled emission change improved kurtosis agreement
with little effect on temporal fit.
